note: Triennial rural district council election. Polling in Fermanagh took place on Wednesday 31 May 1933 and the results were declared on Thursday 1 June. The Drummee division was the only contest in this district. Filed on 1933-05-31, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Fermanagh that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1933-06-01 (verification 5 Nov 2026). The Impartial Reporter of 4 May 1933, p. 5, lists the nominations for twenty-five divisions (added 6 Nov 2026); Monea, a division in 1930 and 1936, is not in the printed list; its member, Thomas Elliott, J.P., is placed there by elimination (see the Monea contest). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected (council-audit, Nov 2026): the round note no longer says Monea is not filled here; gapfill-fermanagh places Thomas Elliott, J.P., there by elimination (Fermanagh Herald, 10 June 1933, p. 5). Renamed from 'Coolyermor' to Coolyermer (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Enniskillen Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Coolyermer; the rounds were filed as Coolyermor (1924, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1955, 1958, 1961); Cooleyermor (1927); Coolyermer (1952); Coolyermore (1964). This round was filed as 'Coolyermor', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (coolyermor) answers with a redirect to this one.
